FLEET.label: Hub
FLEET.blurb: The fleet's home base. It arrives by road, powers itself, and is packed for robots only: no aisle, every cubic metre used.

spots.title: Solar wings
specs: Two wings, top-hinged on the long edges
Container 12 × 430 W ≈ 5.2 kW · trailer 8 × 430 W ≈ 3.4 kW
Both fold down flat over the walls

spots.title: Starlink
specs: Backhaul for the maps app and the live 3D model

spots.title: Drone nest
specs: VTOL pad + quadcopter pad on the roof
Launch and recover with no one on site

spots.title: Doors and ramp
specs: In the carrier lane · container 2.0 m, trailer 3.0 m

spots.title: Container or trailer
specs: 20 ft ISO · 6.06 × 2.44 × 2.59 m · hook-lift truck delivery
16 ft box on tandem axles · towed by a pickup · 4 landing jacks

spots.title: Carriers, loaded
specs: 2 carriers end to end × 16 folded hexapods = 32
1.2 m wide, straight out over the ramp

spots.title: Side rack
specs: Chipper and cargo payloads for the carriers
Hexapod payload modules and spare packs, to the ceiling

spots.title: Chipper payload
specs: Container: in the side rack · trailer: behind the carrier
Drops onto a carrier's deck rails

spots.title: Power and compute
specs: Hexapods charge on the carrier racks

FLEET.label: VTOL
FLEET.blurb: A quad-plane: four lift rotors for roof take-off and landing, a pusher prop and wing for long mapping passes.

spots.title: Lift rotors
specs: 4 × 0.66 m, vertical take-off from the roof pad

FLEET.label: Quadcopter
FLEET.blurb: A Mavic-class drone for close imaging: creek banks, canopy edges and structures the VTOL can't see well.

spots.title: Integrated camera
specs: Global shutter for photogrammetry and splats

FLEET.label: Carrier
FLEET.blurb: A wheeled payload platform. Its main job is moving folded hexapods across the parcel; swap the payload for the chipper, cargo or sensing.

carrier: 1.85 m loaded, clears the container door
Carries hexapods across the parcel; they step off sideways
chipper: Hopper at the back, at hexapod-arm height
Chips stay on site as mulch
Chipping takes 5–15 kW; a hexapod pack is 1.47 kWh
sensor: 1.3 m with lidar and a camera head

spots.title: Nav lidar
specs: Low on the nose, clear of any payload

FLEET.label: Hexapod
FLEET.blurb: A dog-scale walker for rough, steep or delicate ground. Two arms up front, a clear solar lid, a payload on the rear hitch. Legs tuck under to stack.

spots.title: Two arms
specs: Shoulder, elbow, 2-finger gripper on each front corner

mapping: Telescoping mast, lidar + camera at ≈ 0.8 m
Detailed ground scans; folds flat to stack
drone: A micro-drone launches and lands on the hexapod

spots.title: Solar lid
specs: ≈ 50 W peak in full sun, trickle charge

spots.title: Legs
specs: 3 DOF: hip yaw, hip pitch, knee

spots.title: Folds to stack
specs: 0.76 × 0.46 × 0.27 m, legs tucked under the body

spots.title: 360° cameras
specs: Pods set into all four corners

spots.title: Power
specs: 48 V → 400 V across PCB coils → CC/CV, comms in-band

STAGES.label: Plan
STAGES.line: Find the parcel in our maps app, mark the boundary, then pick the hub site and the work zones.

STAGES.label: Deploy
STAGES.line: The hub is set down on a gravel pad: a 20 ft container with solar, Starlink, a radio mast, compute and the robot fleet inside.

STAGES.label: Scan
STAGES.line: The VTOL maps the parcel from 120 m, the quadcopter details the creek from 30 m, and the ATV lidar-scans under the oaks. The 3D model builds on your computer as the data lands.

STAGES.label: Operate
STAGES.line: Hexapods pull the broom the scan found and plant natives in its place; the ATV hauls; the quadcopter watches the cell.
